title: Close seven accessibility and UX findings from the industry-standard review (WCAG 2.1 AA, NN/g heuristics)

approvals.evidence: "You already have priority" (2026-09-06), in response to the assistant naming this batch (the two HIGH frontend findings plus the related MEDIUM/LOW accessibility findings from the same review dimension) as the recommended next item after the security correction.

body.problem: Six-dimension industry-standard review (2026-09-06) confirmed seven accessibility/UX findings, two HIGH: (1) QuickEditPopover.tsx/StatusCellEditor.tsx's required status-change reason field gave a screen-reader user no announcement when a save was refused (WCAG 3.3.1); (2) closing an editor could silently move focus to a non-tabbable cell because useOverlay.ts's unconditional focus-restore-on-unmount overwrote the caller's own focus target (WCAG 2.4.3). Five more in the same dimension: two colour-contrast failures below the 4.5:1 AA floor (--text-faint, --h-atrisk/--sev-medium), the rich-text editor's focus outline removed with no replacement (WCAG 2.4.7), three FilterBar popovers with no Escape dismissal (NN/g consistency), and two disclosure buttons missing aria-expanded (WCAG 4.1.2).

source.reference: Industry-standard review workflow (2026-09-06), six independent reviewers each citing a named external standard, each finding adversarially verified by a separate agent before being reported. This specification's own author additionally found a third contrast failure the review missed (--text-faint in dark theme, 4.16:1) while computing the light-theme fix's exact replacement value.

scope_in: components/QuickEditPopover.tsx and StatusCellEditor.tsx: aria-describedby, aria-invalid and a persistent hint that becomes an announced (role=alert) error after a refused submit attempt on the required reason field

components/useOverlay.ts: the focus-restore-on-unmount cleanup only fires when focus would otherwise be lost (document.activeElement is document.body), not unconditionally, so a caller's own explicit focus target (e.g. TreeGrid's focusRow) is never overwritten

app/globals.css: --text-faint (both light and dark) and --h-atrisk/--sev-medium (light; dark already passed) recomputed to clear the 4.5:1 WCAG 1.4.3 floor, with the real contrast ratio recorded in a comment beside each
app/globals.css: .rte:focus-within gets a border-color change, mirroring the existing .chat-input/.resp-input pattern, replacing the outline .rte-content:focus removes

components/FilterBar.tsx: a shared useDismissOnOutsideOrEscape hook, replacing the three near-duplicate outside-click-only effects for the Columns, More and Legend popovers, adding Escape dismissal to all three without adopting useOverlay's modal (inert/focus-trap) behaviour
components/FilterBar.tsx: aria-expanded added to the Columns and Legend buttons, matching the adjacent More button which already had it
scope_out: Routing the three FilterBar popovers through the modal useOverlay hook (a deliberate scope decision: they are lightweight non-modal dropdowns and gain nothing from inert/tab-trap/focus-restore that a small Escape-and-outside-click handler does not already give them)

The remaining findings from the same review (the HIGH backend migration-pattern finding, the MEDIUM/LOW backend findings, the MEDIUM owner-assignment-override and native-confirm()/search-flash/mirrorError frontend findings) — separate corrections

acceptance_criteria.given: the required status-change reason field is empty
acceptance_criteria.when: the person presses Enter (QuickEditPopover) or the disabled Save path is attempted (StatusCellEditor, which already moves focus to the field)
acceptance_criteria.then: aria-invalid becomes true, a role=alert error is rendered and announced, and the input's aria-describedby continues to point at it

acceptance_criteria.given: an overlay's onClose handler synchronously moves focus to a specific element before the overlay unmounts (TreeGrid's focusRow pattern)
acceptance_criteria.then: the cleanup does not overwrite that focus target, because document.activeElement is no longer document.body at cleanup time

acceptance_criteria.given: an overlay closes with no custom focus-restore call (the ordinary case)
acceptance_criteria.then: focus restores to the original trigger exactly as before this change, because document.activeElement is document.body at cleanup time

acceptance_criteria.given: the --text-faint or --h-atrisk/--sev-medium tokens, in either theme
acceptance_criteria.when: measured against their background with the WCAG relative-luminance formula

acceptance_criteria.given: the Columns, More or Legend popover is open
acceptance_criteria.then: the popover closes, matching every other overlay in the app
its aria-expanded state matches whether its menu is open

business_rules: BR1 (E1, this review). A required field's validation state must be programmatically determinable (aria-invalid) and its error text programmatically associated (aria-describedby) and announced (role=alert) at the moment an attempt is refused — a disabled button's title attribute or a focus move alone does not satisfy this.

BR2 (E1, this review). A hook shared by multiple overlay types must not let one caller's explicit focus intent be silently overwritten by the hook's own default behaviour; a default action fires only when its precondition (focus otherwise lost) actually holds.
